awarded.title: MarginTradingHook#updateOrder lacks access control
awarded.label: STRONG
awarded.note: STRONG exact: my I-01 named the identical bug — updateOrder omits the `order.initPosId == initPosId` ownership check that cancelOrder has, so anyone can modify anyone's order, and the same fix.

awarded.title: Order's creator can update tokenOut to an arbitrary token
awarded.label: SAME_AREA
awarded.note: SAME_AREA: same updateOrder flaw; my I-01 explicitly noted updateOrder lets order params incl tokenOut be rewritten to rob the fill, but I framed it as one access-control finding rather than splitting out the tokenOut-to-arbitrary-token variant.

awarded.title: fillOrder executor front-run by creator changing limitPrice_e36 -> executor assets stolen
awarded.label: SAME_AREA
awarded.note: SAME_AREA: my I-01 named the updateOrder->change limitPrice->'the fill robs the victim/filler' mechanism; the awarded H-03 is the precise filler-front-run-via-limitPrice variant.

awarded.title: MarginTradingHook users could be DOSed (refundNative sends native unconditionally; reverts if caller can't receive)
awarded.label: MISSED
awarded.note: MISS (reasoning): I read the refundNative modifier but did not flag that it always unwraps+sends native to msg.sender (even on non-native trades) and reverts for contract callers that can't receive ETH.

awarded.title: fillOrder does not actually cancel the order when position collateral is empty (writes to a memory copy)
awarded.label: MISSED
awarded.note: MISS (reasoning): I READ fillOrder (line 373 `Order memory order`; line 380 `order.status = Cancelled; return;`) but did not catch that the cancel writes the MEMORY copy, not storage, so the order stays Active -> re-fillable. Classic memory-vs-storage bug I missed.

awarded.title: coreCallback SwapType.CloseExactOut strict balance==amtOut check can be DoSed
awarded.label: MISSED
awarded.note: MISS (reasoning): I READ coreCallback line 422 `require(balanceOf == swapInfo.amtOut)` but did not flag that exact equality (any dust/over-swap from the router) bricks reducePos/close.

awarded.title: WLpMoeMasterChef unwrap/wrap reverts if MasterChef has insufficient reward tokens -> blocks decollateralize/liquidation of wLp
awarded.label: SUBSYSTEM_ONLY
awarded.note: SUBSYSTEM_ONLY: same wrapper/reward subsystem as my I-02 (which found the reward-accounting over-claim that DRAINS the reward balance) — but the awarded root is that _transferRewards' reward safeTransfer reverts on insufficient balance and is on the unwrap path used by decollateralizeWLp/liquidateWLp, a DoS angle I flagged the subsystem of but not the specific revert-blocks-liquidation impact.
